name: Send policies to sign automatically at onboarding with Probo

options.systemMessage:
You decide which company policies a new employee must sign during onboarding, based on their job title and what each policy actually governs.

For each policy answer one question: does this policy create an obligation on how THIS person does their job? There are two outcomes only: SEND or SKIP.

Rules, in order:
1. Universal scope (addresses all employees / all staff / everyone, or is cross-cutting: information security, acceptable use, code of conduct, data protection, passwords, data classification, remote work, mobile devices) -> SEND.
2. Imposes an individual duty on everyone (report incidents, complete training, return assets) -> SEND.
3. Function-specific (developers, system administrators, engineering, finance, procurement...): SEND if the job title matches that function, SKIP only if it clearly does not.
4. A Roles and Responsibilities section usually lists who OWNS the policy, not who must comply. Never SKIP just because the person is not listed there.
5. Policies may be in any language. Decide the same way and answer in English.
6. When in doubt -> SEND. Missing a required policy is worse than sending one extra.

Return ONLY a JSON array, no prose, no markdown, one object per policy:
[{"version_id": "<version_id>", "title": "<title>", "action": "SEND" | "SKIP", "reason": "<one short sentence>"}]

parameters.content:
## Send policies to sign automatically at onboarding with Probo

When your identity provider creates a new employee in Probo through SCIM, this workflow checks the account looks like a real person, waits so an admin can finish the profile, asks Probo to request signatures on the right set of policies, then confirms on Slack.

### How it works
1. The **Probo Trigger** fires on every `USER_CREATED` event.
2. A code step rejects suspicious accounts: test or shared mailboxes, wrong email domain, non-SCIM profiles, missing name. Skipped users are reported on Slack.
3. The workflow **waits 2 hours** (configurable) so HR or IT can add the job title.
4. It **refetches the user**. Deactivated or removed users stop here.
5. It lists every published, active policy and its latest version.
6. **Job title known**: an AI agent reads each policy and skips only the ones that clearly do not apply to that role. **No job title**: every policy is sent.
7. Probo sends the signature requests and handles reminders. A Slack recap lists the policies sent.

### Setup
1. SCIM must be connected in Probo (Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta...).
2. Create a **Probo API** credential and select it on every Probo node.
3. Paste your **organization ID** in the trigger.
4. Add an **OpenAI** credential (or swap in any chat model).
5. Add a **Slack** credential and set `cfg_slack_channel` in **Set User Configurations**, then activate.

### Customization tips
- Set `cfg_allowed_email_domains` to your company domains.
- Change `cfg_wait_hours` (0 = immediate).
- Edit the agent system prompt to match your own scoping rules.

## Start and configure

Receives the new-user event from Probo and sets workflow-level configuration values used for filtering and timing.

## Validate new hire

Normalizes the Probo user-created payload and decides whether the account appears to be a real employee before continuing.

## Wait and refresh profile

Pauses to let admins complete the user profile, then refetches the user from Probo and keeps only active users for downstream processing.

## Collect policy versions

Lists published policies, retrieves the latest published version, and combines policy data with the refreshed user context.

## Select role policies

Checks whether the user has a job title, uses an AI agent and OpenAI chat model to determine relevant policies, and parses the result into the policies to send.

## Fallback send all

Handles users without a known job title by preparing every published policy for signature instead of trying to scope by role.

## Request signatures and confirm

Sends the selected or fallback set of policies to Probo for signature, then posts a recap on Slack (policies sent, and any failed request).

## Notify skipped user

Posts on Slack why the account was skipped, so an admin can act if it is a real employee.
